questions.q: Why do standard browser DevTools (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) work directly for debugging LWC components?
options: LWC compiles down to real JavaScript, HTML, and CSS running in the browser, so the same DevTools used for any web app apply directly
Salesforce ships a dedicated LWC-only debugger that replaces browser DevTools
LWC components cannot be debugged at all outside of Apex debug logs
Browser DevTools only work on Aura components, not LWC
questions.explain: Because LWC produces real browser-native JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, there's no separate Salesforce-specific debugger needed -- the Elements, Console, Sources, and Network panels all work directly.

questions.q: What does enabling Lightning debug mode actually change?
options: It enables live editing of Apex classes directly in the browser
It automatically fixes any bugs found in a component
It serves unminified JavaScript instead of the default minified version, trading some performance for readable stack traces and variable names
It disables all SLDS styling to make DOM inspection easier
questions.explain: By default, Lightning Experience serves minified JavaScript, making stack traces hard to read. Debug mode serves unminified JavaScript instead, at some performance cost, specifically to make debugging easier.

questions.q: Per this lesson's checklist, what is the first thing to check when a component doesn't appear at all in Lightning App Builder?
options: Whether an @track decorator is missing from a field
Whether the component's CSS file has a syntax error
isExposed and <targets> in the js-meta.xml, and whether there was a deploy failure in the CLI output
Whether the component uses lwc:if or if:true
questions.explain: A component failing to appear at all is most often an exposure/targets misconfiguration (Lesson 27) or a failed deployment -- not a rendering or data issue, which is why the checklist starts there.

questions.q: Per this lesson's checklist, what commonly causes a property update to silently fail to re-render?
options: The property is marked @api
The component is exposed to lightning__RecordPage
The component has too many quiz questions
Mutating an object or array in place without @track or without reassigning it to a new value
questions.explain: This is the same reactivity gap covered in Lesson 6 -- mutating an object or array's internals in place, without @track or a full reassignment, does not automatically trigger a re-render.

questions.q: Why does the habit of wrapping imperative Apex calls in try/catch (from Lesson 18) help specifically with debugging?
options: It prevents the Apex method from ever throwing an error in the first place
try/catch blocks automatically open the Sources panel at the point of failure
A caught and logged error gives a clean, readable message (such as error.body.message) in the console, whereas an unhandled rejection can produce a much less helpful generic error
It removes the need to check the Network panel entirely
questions.explain: Catching and logging the error surfaces a specific, readable message in the console. An unhandled rejection, by contrast, often shows up as a vaguer, less actionable error -- making the try/catch habit directly useful for debugging, not just for user-facing error handling.
